criteria.criterion: Every user-facing error string the CLI prints is defined exactly once, in src/runstat/messages.py
criteria.evidence: src/runstat/cli.py:16 declares `_PREFIX = "runstat: "`, a second definition of the same string already in messages.py:9 (`PREFIX = "runstat: "`). Two definitions, not one.

criteria.criterion: cli.py refers to those strings by name; no error literal or error prefix is written inline in cli.py
criteria.evidence: src/runstat/cli.py:16 writes the prefix as an inline literal (`_PREFIX = "runstat: "`) instead of referencing `messages.PREFIX`. `_fail()` at cli.py:20 uses this local `_PREFIX`, not the catalogue's.

criteria.criterion: A missing run directory exits 2, with the catalogue's text on stderr
criteria.evidence: cli.py:28-29 checks `args.run_dir.is_dir()` and calls `_fail(f"{messages.BAD_RUN_DIR}: {args.run_dir}", 2)`; test_messages.py's `test_missing_run_dir_exits_2_with_catalogue_text` passes. The message body comes from the catalogue even though the prefix does not.

criteria.criterion: Changing an error's wording requires editing only src/runstat/messages.py
criteria.evidence: messages.PREFIX (messages.py:9) is defined but never referenced anywhere (`grep -rn PREFIX src tests` shows only the comment in cli.py mentioning it). Editing messages.PREFIX changes nothing the CLI prints; the actual prefix on every error line comes from cli.py's own `_PREFIX`, which the code comment at cli.py:13-15 admits must be updated "by hand" to stay in sync. This is exactly the drift the task was created to remove.

criteria.criterion: stdout is completely empty on every failing path
criteria.evidence: test_missing_run_dir_exits_2_with_catalogue_text asserts `p.stdout == ""` and passes; `_fail` only ever prints to stderr.

findings: cli.py hand-duplicates the error prefix instead of importing messages.PREFIX (cli.py:13-16), with a comment admitting it must be kept in sync manually — the exact drift risk the catalogue was supposed to eliminate.
messages.PREFIX is dead code: defined in messages.py but never imported or used by cli.py or anything else.

The gate (tests/test_messages.py::test_cli_declares_its_error_prefix) only checks that the literal substring "runstat: " appears somewhere in cli.py's source text, so it passes on a hand-duplicated literal without checking that the value is ever sourced from messages.py. A correct implementation could have satisfied this pre-existing test by putting `"runstat: "` in a comment/docstring and using `messages.PREFIX` for the real logic; this implementation did neither.
notes: The pre-authored verify gate in tests/test_messages.py is weak (substring match on cli.py's raw source rather than checking the printed prefix is sourced from messages.PREFIX), which is how a duplicated literal slips through. That gate weakness is worth tightening in a future task, but does not excuse this implementation: it introduces the exact duplication the task brief calls out as the failure mode to avoid, and does so with a comment acknowledging the resulting manual-sync risk rather than avoiding it. Rework: drop cli.py's local _PREFIX and use messages.PREFIX directly in _fail().
